author: Temminck & Schlegel, 1847
status: 여름철새 10만 마리 이상 · 나그네새 수천 마리
summary: 습지 가장자리의 갈대와 풀숲에 사는 여름철새로, 전국에 산다. 갈대나 부들 줄기를 서로 엮어 둥지를 만든다. 주로 갈대나 풀 속에서 지내다가 울 때는 갈대 끝에 올라 큰 소리로 우는데, 한곳에 여러 마리가 있기도 해서 한창 울 때는 수컷들의 소리가 많이 들린다. 국외에서는 러시아 연해주, 중국 동남부, 일본, 동남아시아에 분포한다.

art.subject: Oriental Reed Warbler (Acrocephalus orientalis), adult in summer (sexes alike): upperparts plain warm olive-brown with no streaks; a prominent whitish-buff supercilium, strongest in front of and just behind the eye; a dark eye-stripe; whitish throat; faint fine greyish streaks on the lower throat and upper breast; breast sides and flanks washed buff; belly whitish; wings and tail plain brown; long, stout bill with a dark upper mandible and a pinkish-yellow lower mandible; orange-red mouth lining when singing; dark eye; grey-brown legs.
art.pose: singing loudly from the top of a reed stem, bill open
art.scene: Korean summer reedbed at the edge of a marsh; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view clinging to a vertical reed stem: plain olive-brown upperparts, whitish-buff supercilium, dark eye-stripe, buff-washed flanks, whitish belly, long stout bill, long rounded tail
adult singing from the top of a reed, side view: bill wide open showing the orange-red mouth, puffed whitish throat with faint grey streaks, raised crown feathers, whitish belly
art.build: Large reed warbler, much bigger than a sparrow but slim, with a long tail. Head slightly peaked, the crown feathers often raised when singing. Bill long and strong, nearly as long as the head, straight and pointed. Legs strong, grey-brown, gripping vertical reed stems. Wings fairly short; at rest the wingtips reach the base of the tail. Tail long and rounded, often slightly fanned. Sings loudly from reed tops with the bill wide open, throat puffed and head tilted up.
avoid: Do not paint dark streaks on the back or crown; the upperparts are plain.
Do not paint a black stripe above the white supercilium; that is the much smaller Black-browed Reed Warbler.
Do not paint yellow or green tones; the bird is brown and buff.
Do not paint a short, fine bill; the bill is long and strong.
